To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnitude of differences between ADHD cases with and without comorbid oppositional defiant/conduct disorder (ODD/CD) and typically developing controls is larger in periods of developmental continuity than in periods of developmental transition, and that this pattern holds for executive inhibitory control and delay aversion.
the magnitude of the neuropsychological deficits of ADHD is larger outside transition periods than in transition periods.
ADHD-related deficits are more pronounced outside transition periods of the underlying neuropsychological functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether ADHD-related neuropsychological basic impairments can be detected in the transition period between relative stability and relative change in normative development.
ADHD as a developmental disorder and with the identification of the underlying basic neuropsychological deficits.

the question whether the time windows of the transition periods of the normative development of neuropsycho-logical functions, which are assumed to underly ADHD, are related to the time windows of heightened ADHD prevalence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ADHD is not a neuropsychological deficit disorder but rather a neuropsychologically defined disorder.
ADHD-related IC and DA deficits are not stable over time but show developmental changes that are not necessarily related to the disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developmental course of ADHD-related deficits is a time-window phenomenon.
the ADHD-related basic deficit in executive IC is not stable over the lifespan and that the basic deficit in DA emerges later and may be more specific to ADHD.
ADHD-related basic neuropsychological deficits in the IC and the DA domain are more clearly detectable in age periods of relative developmental continuity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
time windows matter when it comes to the development of neuropsychologically basic functions in children with ADHD and controls.
the time windows in which neuropsychological deficits are assessed matter.
